heading: Oilers linked to blockbuster Dylan Larkin trade as Matthew Savoie-led package puts Detroit in a difficult position
author: Global Sports Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM /  Sep 21, 2026, 17:28 IST
paragraphs: The Edmonton Oilers have been linked to a hypothetical trade for Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin, with a proposed package built around Matthew Savoie
The idea, posted through PuckGM, would send Savoie, Josh Samanski, Beau Akey and Edmonton’s 2028 third-round pick to Detroit for Larkin
It comes at a complicated moment for the Red Wings, who are dealing with Larkin’s trade request but have also made it clear they are not planning a rebuild

Larkin’s contract and full no-trade clause add another layer to a deal that looks far easier to construct on paper than it would be to complete.Could Matthew Savoie-led package be enough for Dylan Larkin?Savoie is the obvious centerpiece of the proposal
The 22-year-old winger was selected ninth overall by Buffalo in 2022 before joining Edmonton in the 2024 Ryan McLeod trade
He just completed his first full NHL season, producing 18 goals and 37 points in 82 games while playing alongside Connor McDavid
That gives Detroit a young player with real NHL experience rather than a prospect who still needs years to develop.The rest of the package is less certain
Samanski appeared in 24 NHL games last season, while Akey remains an intriguing young defenseman who has yet to make his NHL debut and is recovering from shoulder surgery
Add the 2028 third-round pick, and Detroit would receive several pieces, but none offers the immediate production Larkin provides.That matters because Larkin remains a productive center
He has spent his entire 808-game NHL career with Detroit, recording 276 goals and 643 points

He also scored 34 goals and had 67 points in 74 games during the 2025-26 season.Why would the Oilers have trouble making Dylan Larkin work?The biggest obstacle for Edmonton may not be the trade package
It could be the contract.Larkin is signed through 2030-31 at an $8.7 million annual cap hit and has a full no-trade clause
His camp has reportedly circulated a preferred destination list that does not include Edmonton.There is also the roster question
Edmonton already has McDavid and Leon Draisaitl carrying a combined $26.5 million cap hit
Adding Larkin would give the Oilers another expensive center and leave less room for the depth needed around their stars.Detroit faces its own problem

Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has said a rebuild is “out of the question,” while owner Chris Ilitch said, “He could be here all year,” referring to Larkin.That makes the proposed deal especially difficult to square with Detroit’s stated direction
Savoie could become an important player, but moving Larkin for potential rather than established production would change the Red Wings’ timeline
